title: Boiling Water Clears Grease Clogs
description: A common myth in residential drainage is that pouring boiling water clears grease build-up completely. While hot water temporarily liquefies fats, oils, and grease near the sink drain, it rapidly cools as it travels down the branch line. As the water temperature drops, the suspended grease re-solidifies further downstream in cold underground piping or building sewers. This simply relocates the blockage to a much less accessible area, leading to severe main line backups. Professional plumbers rely on mechanical drain cleaning, hydro-jetting, and preventative grease management to safely clear grease accumulation from drainage systems.
